# Bundled third-party redistribution materials

These files supplement the original LICENSE, NOTICE, package metadata and source notices retained in the application. The first-party MIT license does not replace any third-party license.

## Runtime and package inventory

- `python-standalone/sources.json`: CPython 3.12.13, python-build-standalone 20260807, aarch64-apple-darwin pgo+lto. The exact upstream full archive supplied the original Python/native notices. The source archive URL and SHA256 are recorded. The `extensions` inventory distinguishes static links from system libraries. OpenSSL 3.5.7 is static; the macOS ncurses, panel, edit and z links point to system libraries. No Python zstd dylib is bundled in this 3.12 runtime. The complete upstream standalone license directory is retained, including notices for components not selected by this target. `CPYTHON-INCORPORATED-SOFTWARE.rst` is the matching CPython acknowledgements document.
- `python-packages/inventory.json`: all 29 installed Python distributions, package notice paths/hashes, and supplemental notices. Flatbuffers 25.12.19, jieba 0.42.1, loguru 0.7.3 and tokenizers 0.23.2 needed supplemental upstream license files. ONNX Runtime 1.31.0 already contains its LICENSE and ThirdPartyNotices.txt inside its Python package.
- `model/`: pinned BAAI and Qdrant model cards, their revisions, and the FlagEmbedding MIT text linked by the BAAI model card. This covers the public bge-small-zh-v1.5 model; model payload hashes remain in semantic-manifest.json. No personal embedding index is a model artifact.
- `npm/sources.json`: supplemental license locations for npm packages that omitted separate root files. Data-uri-to-buffer retains the full MIT grant in its existing README. dfa, fontkit and brotli declare MIT in their exact upstream README/package metadata but omit a separate full grant/copyright file. Their upstream declarations and authors are preserved; standard unmodified MIT terms are also supplied at `codex-tools/MIT-standardized-terms/MIT.txt`. No missing copyright year has been invented. Brotli's bundled Google Apache-2.0 source notices are additionally retained. For several packages whose npm metadata omitted gitHead, the notice provenance is recorded separately and is not represented as proof of their source revision.
- `codex-tools/`: ripgrep 15.1.0 MIT/Unlicense and its PCRE2 10.45 license. Codex CLI 0.144.6 retains the separately provided Apache-2.0 LICENSE and NOTICE in the application. Node retains its distribution LICENSE, and Electron/Chromium retain their own notices.
- LibreOffice's existing engine package already supplies `licenses/`, `sources/core-source.json`, full changes/patches and its upstream revision. Those original materials must remain in the package; this supplementary folder does not replace them.

## Native LGPL and GPL components and actual sources

The same GitHub Release must include the separate corresponding `third-party-sources` archive. Its contents are staged separately from Git; `sources-index.json` records every downloaded file and SHA256.

- `sharp-libvips/sources.json`: @img/sharp-libvips-darwin-arm64 1.3.4 / libvips 8.18.7. All 28 upstream source archives plus the exact v1.3.4 build scripts and referenced patches are supplied, along with sharp 0.35.5 wrapper source for rebuilding/relinking the native addon. The exact macOS build recipe is in the upstream source archive (`build/posix.sh`, `build.sh`, `versions.properties`, and the darwin platform files). LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 texts and upstream component notices are retained here. The non-target sharp-wasm32 package is excluded from this macOS arm64 release; no unpinned wasm-vips source is claimed.
- `sharp-libvips/rust-sources.json`: all 357 registry package sources from the original librsvg 2.63.2 Cargo.lock are supplied; every crate was verified against the lockfile checksum. This is an explicit source superset. The upstream recipe edits disabled features and runs `cargo update --workspace`; we did not reconstruct the upstream builder's final lockfile, and do not claim a byte-for-byte reproduction of its dylib.
- `sherpa-onnx/sources.json`: the bundled native library reports sherpa-onnx 1.13.8, git 11afbd00 and ONNX Runtime 1.28.2 through its exported runtime APIs. The full matching sherpa source commit and 11 exact CMake dependency archives are supplied, with CMake SHA256 verification when provided. The full source archive includes the Node-addon build workflow and build flags; selected recipes are also retained under `sherpa-onnx/build/`.
- Sherpa statically incorporates eSpeak NG from commit ed530aa113046142eb5115cf2fc9157854d0ffe1. That component carries GPLv3; its full exact source archive and COPYING text are included. Piper-phonemize and the other source dependencies retain their own notices. The upstream Node-addon recipe uses shared sherpa libraries with TTS enabled by default; espeak/piper are statically linked into the sherpa library. This binary must not be described as wholly MIT.
- The second ONNX Runtime, 1.28.2 used by sherpa, has separate matching LICENSE and ThirdPartyNotices.txt under `npm/sherpa-onnx-darwin-arm64/onnxruntime-1.28.2/`; these do not substitute for the Python runtime's 1.31.0 notices.

These are evidence-backed attribution and source materials, not a legal opinion or an assertion that all third-party builds have been independently reproduced. The source archives, matching notices, application source and build/installation instructions should remain available with the release. Any later dependency or binary change requires refreshing the inventory and source hashes.
